reasons: Dr. Perf did not produce an irregularity value

attempts.hypothesis: Instruction count is approximately a fixed call cost plus an insertion-path overhead and a linear cost per newly cached full block.

pcvs.name: new_full_blocks
pcvs.rationale: Counts newly completed blocks requiring hash assignment and prefix-cache insertion in this single-group workload.

pcvs.name: has_new_full_blocks
pcvs.rationale: Captures the fixed cost of entering block-cache insertion instead of taking the no-new-blocks path.

attempts.hypothesis: This workload consistently takes the no-new-full-blocks path, so instruction count should be approximately constant across token counts. A token-count PCV supplies the state diversity needed to test that hypothesis.

pcvs.name: tokens_to_cache
pcvs.rationale: Provides distinct entry states across prompt and decode lengths; the previous measurement showed that every call had zero newly completed cache blocks.

attempts.hypothesis: With no newly completed cache blocks, cost is largely constant. Grouping by generation progress should capture any prefill/decode differences and reduce the influence of isolated startup overhead in sparsely observed prompt-length states.

pcvs.name: output_tokens
pcvs.rationale: A cheap request-lifecycle cardinality that distinguishes prefill and successive decode stages while pooling calls across prompt lengths.
